title: Narrate between the sections of a long text
statement: Narrate a long text read in parts: open each part with a short line on what to watch for, review it afterwards, and summarise at the end.
example: The same format note heads all four reading texts of one Grade 9 unit.
detail: Every reading text in a Grade 9 unit opens with a format note: a narrator speaks between sections, feeding forward before a section, reviewing back after it and summarising at the end, while section headings stay hidden and a simple divider marks each break. The forward feeds point readers at what to look for, such as deciding whether to believe a speaker or looking for one word.
against: Some forward feeds also tell learners what the next section contains before they read it: "In this next section, you'll read that Othello turned those men down and chose someone else." (`g9/sources/Act 1 reading texts/Act 1/1. 1.1 - Iago_s Introduction - Text.docx`, line 38), which the record `no-spoilers-of-what-comes-later` forbids. A ruling of 30 September deleted the lines from four of the course's lessons and one in another course because "They take away from the reading flow." (kb-0230-late-sept-incidental-findings.qmd lines 39-46), and they lengthen the timed read-through (REGISTER-2026-09-15.md line 181).
